title: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight
hook: after Karna, an old teacher pleads for peace, and Duryodhana says no
tomorrow: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight

segments.voice: Yesterday: Karna died beside his stuck wheel, with Krishna's questions still in the air and a light rising into the sun. Your line was he hangs his head in shame, and says nothing.

Karna is gone. Bhishma lies on his bed of arrows. Drona is dead. The commanders Duryodhana trusted have fallen one after another, and in the Kaurava camp the king sits among the survivors, grieving. Then an old man speaks up. It's Kripa, the teacher who trained these princes when they were boys, Kaurava and Pandava alike. He doesn't flatter. He tells the king the truth as he sees it.
screen: `KARNA IS GONE.` → `THE COMMANDERS HAVE FALLEN.` → `KRIPA SPEAKS.`

segments.voice: Kripa's counsel, in Ganguli's English, is plain: make peace with the Pandavas. Yudhishthira is gentle, he says in effect. He'll let you keep a share of the kingdom. There's still time. And Duryodhana says no. His reasons are worth hearing, because he isn't simply stubborn. He has wronged the Pandavas too deeply, he says, to be trusted now; they would never believe a peace from him. Then something closer to the bone. My friends died for me, the kings and kinsmen who fought at my word. How could I now live in comfort, after sending them to die? He would rather fall the way they fell, as a warrior on the field. It's a terrible answer and, in its way, a loyal one. Then the question: who leads tomorrow? Drona's son Ashvatthama names Shalya, king of Madra, the man who drove Karna's chariot and told him he was the crow. Duryodhana asks him, and Shalya accepts. The driver becomes the commander, and this book of the epic is named for him: the Shalya Parva. The twins' own uncle, who came to the war meaning to fight for their side, will lead the army against them.
screen: `KRIPA SAYS MAKE PEACE` · `TOO LATE TO BE TRUSTED` · `MY FRIENDS DIED FOR ME` · then, large: `SHALYA TAKES COMMAND`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a road you've stayed on longer than you meant to, because turning back would mean admitting something. Only in your mind, picture one step back the way you came, and notice what happens in your chest and shoulders. Nothing to decide now; if you pray, you can bring that road into your prayer.
Shalya. King of Madra, the twins' uncle, Karna's driver, and now the commander of the Kaurava army, after Duryodhana refuses peace.
Your line: it isn't too late. Kripa said it, and Duryodhana couldn't hear it. That's day eight hundred forty-three.

howItsDone: The Shalya Parva, the epic's book named for Shalya, is read and recited with the rest of the Mahabharata; Kripa's plea for peace and Duryodhana's refusal are retold as a turning point before the war's last day.

fork.setup: you're Duryodhana. your commanders have fallen, and your old teacher Kripa urges you to make peace. what do you do?
options: send word to Yudhishthira and make peace.
refuse, and name a new commander.
leave the field and go into the forest.
fork.reveal: Duryodhana refuses: he can't be trusted now, and he won't live in comfort after his friends died for him. Shalya takes command.

original.note: Shalya: king of Madra, Karna's charioteer, and the Kauravas' new commander.

trapdoor: what you thought: Duryodhana kept fighting out of pure pride.
what it means: he gives reasons: he can't be trusted now, and he owes his dead friends the same end they met.
what a scholar hears: the epic gives its villain a loyal, grieving logic at this moment, which makes his refusal harder to dismiss.
